description: #EXP-1674 (L2): A BARE IN-APP URL IN AGENT PROSE reads as the chip of what it names. `chipBareAppLinks(text, origin, team, resolve)` runs on DISPLAY text only (agent prose: chat text, narration, steering feeds), never on anything that serializes (descriptions, comments and their editors keep their bytes). Locked ×4: web lib/prose-links.ts, desktop domain::prose_links, iOS ExpCore ProseLinks.swift, Android domain/ProseLinks.kt. THE SCAN, line by line: a line whose first non-space characters (at most 3 spaces) are three backticks or tildes opens a fence, closed by a line starting the same way; fenced lines stay as written (an unclosed fence runs to the end). In other lines a run of n backticks opens a code span closed by the next run of exactly n (no such run = plain text); a span stays as written. Elsewhere a candidate starts at `http://` or `https://` (any case) whose previous character is not an ASCII word character, `[`, `<`, or the `(` of `](`; it runs up to an ASCII space, tab or any of `<>()[]`"'`, then drops trailing `.,;:!?*_~`. THE RULE: `classifyAppLink(url, origin, team)` names it, its teamSlug must equal `team` (case-insensitive; no team = no chips): issue + issueRef = kind `issue` (id = identifier), board = `board` (id = boardSlug), session + chat = `session` (id = the session id), agent = `agent` (id = agentId); anything else stays a plain link. `resolve(kind, id)` = the display title of a SYNCED row, null otherwise; null stays a plain link (fixture `synced`, keys `kind:id`). THE OUTPUT: an issue = `#<identifier as written>`, which every client's existing chip pass draws as THE IssueChip with its title and status glyph. Any other kind = a labelled link `[<title>](<url without its hash>#exp-chip-<kind>)`, whose run every markdown renderer paints as THE EntityChip (entity-chip.json: `entityRefIcon` glyph, the title); `\`, `[`, `]`, `*`, `_`, backtick and `~` in the title are backslash-escaped. `proseChipKind(href)` reads the marker back (`chipKindCases`): the text after the LAST `#exp-chip-` when it is `board`, `session` or `agent`, else null. Route kinds drop the hash on open (app-link.json), so the marker never reaches a screen. A labelled link stays the agent's text in link style; a `~/` link in markdown is a labelled link like any other and survives every parser and editor unchanged (CONTRACT_FIXTURES `team_link`).
